title: PartitionValue
description: A single equivalence class or boundary class of one input dimension, owned by exactly one InputSpacePartition. It is defined by a boundary condition and by a representative value that stands for every value in the class during test design. Use InputSpacePartition instead when you are modelling the whole input field or dimension and its complete set of classes, rather than one class within it. Use InputSelection instead when you are binding a specific concrete test datum, used by a particular TestCaseSketch, to one of the partition's classes. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when you are stating which classes of a partition a CoverageRequirement must or must not exercise. Use OutcomeCategory instead when the category classifies expected results (success, validation error, timeout) rather than input values.

label.description: Short identifier for the class, unique within its parent partition (e.g. 'empty-string', 'above-max'); other nodes cite it in coverValues, excludeValues and affectedValues, so it is always set.

description.description: Optional free-text explanation of why values in this class are expected to behave alike and what behaviour they probe; set it when the label and constraint alone do not make the intent clear.

constraint.description: Human-readable description of the condition this partition boundary represents (e.g., 'must be between 0 and 100', 'must not be null or empty').

constraintExpression.description: Machine-evaluable expression encoding the partition boundary condition (e.g., a regex pattern, JSONPath predicate, or comparison expression such as 'value >= 0 && value <= 100').

category.description: Equivalence partition category for this value

representativeValue.description: One abstract value, written as a string, that stands for the whole class in test design (e.g. '101' for above-max, '' for null-empty); it is distinct from the concrete datum later bound in InputSelection.concreteValue.

x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Level Test Design Specification, features and input specification refinement; equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-4 §5.2.1 and §5.2.3
x-dr-evidence: A parametrized test table for a single argument whose case ids name input classes, e.g. @pytest.mark.parametrize ids=['valid','empty','too_long','negative'] or a JUnit @ValueSource/@CsvSource grouped by class.

Test data constants or builder functions named after a class of one field and mirroring a schema constraint, e.g. MAX_LEN_BOUNDARY = 255, invalid_email(), or a 'min - 1' value derived from a minimum declared in the OpenAPI or JSON Schema.
A property-based generator restricted to one class of an input, e.g. a Hypothesis strategy such as st.integers(min_value=0, max_value=100) or a fast-check arbitrary filtered by a regex predicate.
